answer: Fake crowds need work that splits. A sequential, memory-hard cipher chain refuses to split. Each applicant runs two million cipher rounds from a seed tied to one key, each round feeding the next; one pass takes ten minutes. A verifier checks prism checkpoints, fixed heights where the state must match, in seconds. Chains from one source link: each extra identity seeds from a ripple off the previous final state, and its rounds double. Ten fakes cost 10, then 20, then 40 minutes, 5,120 for the tenth. Twenty need about 19 years. It is a corridor that doubles for every copy of you walking it.
